 (BY SHRI ATMARAM BEN - DY. GOVERNMENT ADVOCATE)
 This application coming on for admission this day, the   following:
 ORDER

This is third bail application filed by the applicant under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of regular bail relating to FIR/Crime No.42/2019 dated 12.03.2019 registered at Police Station Gaurihar, District Chhatarpur for the offence under Sections 363, 366A, 344, 376,
376(D), 34 and 506 of IPC and Section 5/6 of POCSO Act.

His first application i.e. M.Cr.C.No.48629/2020 was dismissed as withdrawn vide order dated 20.01.2021 and second application i.e. M.Cr.C.No.14939/2021 was dismissed on merits vide order dated 02.07.2021
Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the crime in question.

He further submits that two other co-accused persons namely Ghanshyam Kushwaha and Ramratan Kushwaha have been granted bail vide orders dated 09.12.2019 and 06.01.2020 i n M.Cr.C.No.50834/2019 and M.Cr.C.No.53767/2019 b y the Ramprkash Kushwaha vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104133485/
1 Co-ordinate Bench of this High Court.

sentences.text: He also submits that prosecutrix is a consenting party.
Applicant does not have any criminal past.
Investigation is complete and charge-sheet has already been filed.
The applicant is in custody since 13.11.2019 and trial will take considerable time to conclude.
He further submits that applicant is permanent resident of district and there is no likelihood of his absconding from the clutches of law or tamper with prosecution evidence.
He also submits that the applicant is ready to furnish adequate surety and shall abide by all the directions and conditions which may be imposed by this Hon'ble Court.
Upon these grounds, the applicant may be released on bail.
Learned counsel for the State has opposed the bail application.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.
In this third bail application, the applicant has prayed for bail on the ground that co-accused persons have been given the benefit of bail and applicant is in custody for almost 4 years.

The bail orders passed in M.Cr.C.No.50834/2019 and M.Cr.C.No.53767/2019 relating to co-accused persons reflect that their case is not identical to the case of present applicant because he is the main perpetrator of crime whose earlier bail application has been rejected on merits.
There is no change in circumstance to reconsider the question of liberty.
Looking to the above facts and circumstances of the case, this Court is not inclined to grant bail to the applicant.
Accordingly, this M.Cr.C. is dismissed.

(ANURADHA SHUKLA) JUDGE Nitesh Ramprkash Kushwaha vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104133485/
